- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) or flat (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% if recent price is trending down.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above prior peak or use 3-period moving average.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to correct; apply mean reversion to last 5–7 days’ average for next 3–5 periods.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5 days; if above, reduce by 1–3% for next 3 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” (neutral), model tends to drift toward historical mean; use 10-day rolling mean as anchor for correction.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes are common; apply “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day after sentiment drops below 0.33.
